bottleneck: Brain imaging routinely finds neural correlates of consciousness, but correlation is not causation: stimulating or lesioning a correlated region does not prove it generates experience rather than merely reflecting it. Disentangling the true neural basis from prerequisites and consequences of consciousness requires causal interventions that are mostly impossible in healthy humans for ethical reasons. The field thus accumulates correlates without converging on mechanisms, and each new imaging study adds another correlate to an already crowded map.
current_state: Perturbation methods (TMS, stimulation) and no-report paradigms chip at the problem, but the causal core of consciousness remains unidentified. Progress is incremental and contested.

title: Consciousness correlates lack causal proof
why_it_blocks: Medicine and brain-machine interfaces need causal levers, not correlations. Without causal mechanisms, treatments for disorders of consciousness remain empirical guesswork, and patients in vegetative states cannot be reliably assessed or helped.
